section_summary: This section contains exhibition pamphlet material, forms and plans for the 1933 Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition in Tokyo. State Department correspondence records efforts to encourage private American participation, the availability of tax-free entry for exhibits, and reports from the exhibition’s American Day. The final page opens a jacket for the 1935 Yokohama Municipal Exposition.

subfiles.title: Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition: suggestions, regulations and exhibit list
subfiles.about: The exhibition solicits foreign contributions and sets out rules for exhibits.
subfiles.summary: The excerpt begins midway through requests for gifts, songs, flags and goods for sale. It then specifies exhibit categories, space charges, display dimensions, shipment through Yokohama, admission and conduct rules, and a 76-group classification of goods.

subfiles.title: Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition: cover and contents
subfiles.about: The cover announces the Ueno Park exhibition for March 17 to May 10, 1933.
subfiles.summary: Cover and contents identify the Tokyo exhibition, its office and the pamphlet sections.

subfiles.title: Fragment of Jefferson Caffery letter on Japanese mission
subfiles.about: Caffery identifies three Japanese mission members and says they will visit other South American countries.
subfiles.summary: Names Maruyama, Amari and Ichikawa as mission members and notes further travel.

subfiles.title: Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition pamphlet and application
subfiles.about: The pamphlet explains the exhibition’s aims, names its supporters and gives foreign exhibitors detailed guidance.
subfiles.summary: It lists Japanese officials and foreign diplomats as patrons or supporters, then presents President Hayashi’s introduction and Kurahashi’s requests for foreign displays and gifts. Repeated suggestions, surviving regulations and a 76-group exhibit list address participation, shipping, space and sales. The final page is an application for exhibition space.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on Yokohama Municipal Exposition
subfiles.about: A State Department officer favors American participation but advises awaiting formal notice of the exposition’s status.
subfiles.summary: Favors participation, pending formal notification and clarification of the exposition’s sponsorship.

subfiles.title: Label for exhibit
subfiles.about: A blank label records an exhibit’s number, article, origin, exhibitor and price.
subfiles.summary: Blank exhibit label with fields for identification and price.

subfiles.title: Plans of Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition grounds
subfiles.about: Two plans show the exhibition grounds at Ueno Park for the 1933 event.
subfiles.summary: Maps locate exhibition buildings and the grounds around Ueno Park landmarks.

subfiles.title: Letter to John Barton Payne on exhibition invitation
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The State Department forwards Japan’s invitation and exhibition pamphlet information to the American Red Cross.
subfiles.summary: Forwards the invitation and descriptive pamphlet extracts to Payne.

subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary of Commerce on exhibition participation
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State requests recommendations and promotion of private American participation because official funding is unavailable.
subfiles.summary: The letter forwards Japan’s invitation and pamphlet extracts, notes that Congress has provided no appropriation for official participation, and asks Commerce to alert interested private exhibitors.

subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary of Labor on exhibition participation
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State requests recommendations and help reaching private American exhibitors.
subfiles.summary: The letter forwards Japan’s invitation, explains the absence of official participation funds, and asks Labor to publicize opportunities to private organizations.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on private exhibition participation
subfiles.about: The division recommends encouraging private American representation at the Tokyo exhibition.
subfiles.summary: With no appropriation for official exhibits, the division sees private participation as a means to sustain American influence, improve sentiment and possibly promote sales.

subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary of the Interior on exhibition participation
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State requests recommendations and help reaching private American exhibitors.
subfiles.summary: The letter forwards Japan’s invitation, explains the absence of official participation funds, and asks Interior to publicize opportunities to private organizations.

subfiles.title: Labor Department reply on exhibition participation
subfiles.about: Labor cannot fund an exhibit but will inform private organizations about the exhibition.
subfiles.summary: Declines departmental participation for lack of funds and offers to notify private organizations.

subfiles.title: Document file note on exhibition in Japan
subfiles.about: The note directs readers to another file concerning the exhibition in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to file 894.00-P.R./57 for exhibition material.

subfiles.title: Miscellaneous report item on Women’s and Children’s International Exhibition
subfiles.about: A report describes the planned 1933 exhibition and organizers’ requests for international participation.
subfiles.summary: Notes the organizers, Education Department support, proposed patrons and appeal to foreign governments.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department reply on exhibition publicity
subfiles.about: Commerce will publicize the exhibition through press and trade channels.
subfiles.summary: Promises a press announcement and notices in Commerce bulletins and trade letters.

subfiles.title: Interior Department reply on exhibition publicity
subfiles.about: Interior lacks participation funds but has notified educators and plans broader publicity.
subfiles.summary: Reports notices to western school officials, educational magazines and women’s organizations.

subfiles.title: American Red Cross reply declining exhibition participation
subfiles.about: The American Red Cross declines the invitation because it lacks exhibit material and resources.
subfiles.summary: Declines participation because suitable material and staff capacity are unavailable.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Ambassador Grew on American exhibition publicity
subfiles.from: W. R. Castle Jr., for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State reports how federal departments are informing potential American exhibitors.
subfiles.summary: The instruction summarizes outreach by Interior, Labor and Commerce to educators, organizations, the press and trade contacts. It reiterates that Congress supplied no funds for official representation.

subfiles.title: Grew despatch forwarding exhibition customs letter
subfiles.about: Grew forwards notice that foreign exhibits may enter Japan without tax or deposit.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the exhibition secretary’s letter announcing free entry for foreign exhibits.

subfiles.title: Kurahashi letter on free entry of foreign exhibits
subfiles.about: The exhibition secretary announces tax-free import of foreign exhibits and asks for participation.
subfiles.summary: Announces free import and asks exhibitors to label packing cases for the exhibition.

subfiles.title: Notice to Secretary of Commerce on free entry of exhibits
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State asks Commerce to tell exhibitors about free entry and packing-case labels.
subfiles.summary: Relays tax-free entry arrangements and the required exhibition destination label.

subfiles.title: Notice to Secretary of Labor on free entry of exhibits
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State asks Labor to tell exhibitors about free entry and packing-case labels.
subfiles.summary: Relays tax-free entry arrangements and the required exhibition destination label.

subfiles.title: Notice to Secretary of the Interior on free entry of exhibits
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: State asks Interior to tell exhibitors about free entry and packing-case labels.
subfiles.summary: Relays tax-free entry arrangements and the required exhibition destination label.

subfiles.title: Interior Department reply on further exhibition publicity
subfiles.about: Interior sees no need for more publicity about free entry and reports no known participants.
subfiles.summary: Previous notices directed inquiries to exhibition officials; the Office of Education knows of no intended participants.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on Grew’s American Day despatch
subfiles.about: A file note highlights Grew’s account of the enthusiastic American Day audience.
subfiles.summary: Calls attention to Grew’s confidential observations and attached speech.

subfiles.title: Grew despatch on American Day at the exhibition
subfiles.about: Grew reports the March 19 American Day ceremony and assesses the audience’s response.
subfiles.summary: Grew describes American flags, a guard of honor, his broadcast speech and presentation of two American dolls. In a confidential section, he calls the audience’s enthusiasm unusually warm while reflecting on how public sentiment might be influenced by official preparation and anti-American propaganda.

subfiles.title: Grew’s congratulatory message at American Day exercises
subfiles.about: Grew congratulates the organizers and presents an American flag and two dolls.
subfiles.summary: The speech praises the exhibition’s aims of home education, domestic economy and international friendship. Grew thanks the organizers for American Day and presents the flag and dolls as symbols of American interest.

subfiles.title: Yokohama Municipal Exposition jacket
subfiles.about: A jacket identifies the Yokohama exposition scheduled for March 24 to May 26, 1935.
subfiles.summary: File jacket records the exposition subject, dates and filing date.
